caseStudy.title: EmberWorks
caseStudy.background:
EmberWorks receives daily equipment logs in a Python HTTP Function. Requests must return quickly with a status location. A bounded worker execution is preferable to a continuously running worker when the queue is empty. The processing team estimates that a message can outlive an individual PeekLock.

The data team stores per-company job status in Cosmos DB. The application sometimes creates a job and immediately queries status from the same SDK session. A 429 alarm occurred during a short ingestion spike. The team does not want users to see cross-company results.

The operator wants trace correlation between acceptance and background work without placing authentication headers in telemetry.

exhibits.title: Workload requirements
exhibits.code:
HTTP p95 acceptance target: 250 ms
Worker task duration: 3–12 minutes
Worker capacity when queue is empty: zero
Cosmos partition key: /companyId

questions.explanation: A queue scaler can observe the broker while the container has zero replicas. A CPU rule cannot measure a nonexistent replica.
options: Use an HTTP rule with concurrentRequests 1
Use a CPU utilization rule without a queue trigger
Increase maxReplicas without setting an event-driven rule
Use a Service Bus KEDA scale rule with minReplicas 0

questions.prompt: The desert sender retried within the broker duplicate detection window. Which message property must stay unchanged on an unpartitioned queue?
questions.answer: message_id
questions.explanation: Duplicate detection uses the application-assigned MessageId. Sequence numbers and delivery counts are set by the broker.
options: sequence_number
delivery_count
locked_until_utc
message_id
